failure_summary.description: The clue 'the Denver type of this' asks for the generic dish noun that the modifier attaches to ('Denver omelet' -> 'Omelet'). The passages even contained 'Egg White Denver Omelet'. The agent instead picked a prominent branded product (Egg White Delight McMuffin) that matched only the cholesterol/egg-white theme and never the 'Denver' modifier.

patch.reasoning: The skill covers 'this X' referents and 'one of these <role>', but not the 'the <Modifier> type/style/version/variety of this' pattern. In that pattern the modifier (a place, name or adjective) is an anchor and the answer is the generic head noun it combines with in a standard compound. The agent should search the passages for '<Modifier> + noun' collocations and answer with the bare noun. It should not choose a thematically related branded item that lacks the modifier. This edit is narrow and general, and does not repeat any previously rejected broad edits.

edits.target: asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'The <Modifier> type / style / version / kind / variety of this' ('the Denver type of this', 'the Boston version of this', 'the Manhattan kind of this') names a standard compound whose head noun is the answer. Search the passages for '<Modifier> <noun>' (e.g. 'Egg White Denver Omelet', 'Denver omelet') and answer with the bare generic noun ('Omelet'), not the modifier and not a branded or themed product from the passages. A candidate must contain or fit the clue's distinctive modifier. A brand item such as 'Egg White Delight McMuffin' that matches only the side theme (cholesterol, egg whites) is wrong. Other clue details (diet, ingredient, cooking method) are just conditions on the generic dish.
